title: A Hen Has Eggs
learning_objectives: Learn that a hen keeps eggs warm and a chick hatches from an egg
Use the words hatch and chick

factual_claims.claim: A hen sits on her eggs to keep them warm.
factual_claims.source: RSPCA (UK), 'Chickens: breeding and incubation' (rspca.org.uk); Britannica Kids, 'Chicken'

factual_claims.claim: A chick uses its beak to break out of the egg; this is called hatching.
factual_claims.source: Britannica Kids, 'Chicken' (hatching); Mississippi State University Extension, 'Hatching eggs' (egg tooth on the beak)

factual_claims.claim: Chicken eggs hatch after about three weeks (21 days) of warmth.
factual_claims.source: Mississippi State University Extension, 'Incubating and hatching chicken eggs' (21-day incubation)

factual_claims.claim: A newly hatched chick is wet and dries into soft fluffy down.
factual_claims.source: Mississippi State University Extension, 'Incubating and hatching chicken eggs'

parent_prompts: Before reading: What comes out of an egg?
After page 3: Why does the hen sit so long? What is she keeping warm?
After reading: How does the chick get out? Tell me with your hands.

pages.illustration_brief: A brown hen standing over a nest with four cream eggs.

vocabulary.example: The hen has soft brown feathers.

pages.text: The hen sits on the eggs. She keeps them warm.
pages.illustration_brief: The hen settled down on the nest, feathers puffed, eyes half closed.
pages.audio_script: The hen sits on the eggs. She keeps them warm.

pages.text: She sits for many days. Day and night.
pages.illustration_brief: Two small scenes side by side: the hen on the nest under a sun, and under a moon.
pages.audio_script: She sits for many days. Day and night.

pages.illustration_brief: Close-up of one egg with a small crack; tiny tap marks.

pages.text: A chick pecks a hole. It pushes out. It hatches!
pages.illustration_brief: A wet chick half out of the broken shell, beak first.
pages.audio_script: A chick pecks a hole. It pushes out. It hatches!

vocabulary.example: The baby turtle hatches on the beach.

pages.text: The chick is wet. Soon it is dry and fluffy. Peep!
pages.illustration_brief: A fluffy yellow chick standing beside the hen; broken shell pieces nearby.
pages.audio_script: The chick is wet. Soon it is dry and fluffy. Peep!

quiz.prompt: Why does the hen sit on the eggs?
quiz.explanation: Page 2 says: She keeps them warm.

quiz.prompt: How does the chick get out of the egg?

options.text: It pecks a hole and pushes

quiz.explanation: Page 5 says: A chick pecks a hole. It pushes out.

quiz.prompt: In this book, what does hatches mean?
quiz.explanation: Page 5: the chick pushes out of the egg. It hatches.

quiz.prompt: What happens right after the tapping sound?
quiz.explanation: Page 4 is the tapping. Page 5 the chick pecks a hole. Being fluffy comes last, on page 6.

quiz.prompt: Tell a grown-up how a chick comes out of an egg. Use the word hatch.
quiz.rubric: not yet: says egg or chick only; with support: two steps with prompting; independent: hen keeps eggs warm, chick pecks and pushes out, gets dry and fluffy
quiz.explanation: Explaining the steps in own words shows understanding of the process.

items.text: The hen keeps the eggs warm.
Tap, tap from inside the egg.
The chick is dry and fluffy.

activities.prompt: Match the word to its meaning.

off_screen_prompt: Curl up small like a chick in an egg. Then tap, tap, and push out! Show someone.
